title: Microsoft Reverses Course on RAM, Says 8GB Is Enough for Windows 11
excerpt: After years of pushing 16GB as the baseline for its AI-first vision, Microsoft now sells budget Surface devices with 8GB — but reviews show Windows 11 still struggles with less memory.
body:
• Microsoft has launched 8GB Surface Laptop and Surface Pro configurations starting at $849, reversing years of recommending 16GB as the minimum for a smooth Windows 11 experience.
  • The shift is driven by soaring DRAM prices — contract costs rose up to 98% in Q1 2026 — as AI infrastructure devours memory supply, forcing manufacturers toward cheaper configurations.
  • Early reviews show the 8GB Surface Laptop freezes during Teams calls and consumes 6.7GB of its 7.6GB available memory under normal use, undermining Microsoft's claims.

Microsoft has quietly reversed one of its most persistent hardware recommendations. After spending two years positioning 16GB of RAM as the mandatory floor for modern Windows 11 PCs — a push tied directly to its Copilot+ AI branding — the company now says 8GB is sufficient for everyday computing.

The updated Surface Laptop page on the Microsoft Store describes 8GB of RAM as "great for everyday use like browsing, streaming, schoolwork, and productivity apps." The previous 16GB recommendation has been dropped, though Microsoft still requires 16GB to access its Copilot+ AI features.

The shift materialized in June 2026 with the launch of new budget Surface devices: a 12-inch Surface Pro at $849 and a 13-inch Surface Laptop at $949, both equipped with first-generation Snapdragon X Plus processors and 8GB of LPDDR5x memory.

A Market Forced by Rising Prices

The reversal did not happen in a vacuum. Traditional DRAM prices have surged as the AI industry's appetite for high-bandwidth memory squeezes supply for consumer devices. According to TrendForce, traditional DRAM contract costs jumped 93% to 98% in Q1 2026, with a further 58% to 63% increase in Q2. The result: every gigabyte now costs manufacturers significantly more, making 16GB configurations harder to fit into budget laptops.

"Customer needs vary by workload, and 8GB configurations give customers another entry point for everyday productivity, browsing, communication, and entertainment."

— Microsoft spokesperson, via PCWorld

Brett Ostrum, Microsoft's corporate vice president of Surface devices, told PCWorld that the company intended to make a "step change" in pricing — raising prices sharply and suddenly rather than gradually. The cheaper Surface models were designed to address a widening gap in the market, where premium devices push past $3,000 while budget buyers are left behind.

Reviews Tell a Different Story

The marketing may say 8GB is enough, but testing suggests otherwise. A review by The Verge found that the 8GB Surface Laptop would "hang or freeze for several seconds" whenever someone joined a Microsoft Teams video call — with just 10 Chrome tabs, Slack, and Signal running in the background.

Windows Task Manager showed the device using approximately 6.7GB of its 7.6GB of available memory under typical workloads. Even after a clean reboot with no unnecessary startup apps, memory usage sat at 4.2GB, climbing to 5.5GB after opening half a dozen browser tabs. Random freezes occurred multiple times per day while working in Google Docs.

The performance gap becomes sharper when compared to Apple's $599 MacBook Neo, which also ships with 8GB but handles similar workloads far more smoothly. Apple's advantage lies in its unified memory architecture and tight software-hardware integration — macOS uses significantly less RAM than Windows for the same tasks, according to testing by Tom's Guide.

As PCWorld observed: consumers tend to ask Apple "how good is it?" For Microsoft, the question is more likely to be "how bad is it going to be?"

What's Next

Microsoft says it is working to reduce Windows 11's memory footprint through what it calls the Windows K2 initiative. Planned optimizations include a smaller default memory baseline, faster memory release when applications are not in use, and migrating core components like the Start menu to WinUI 3 for better responsiveness.

"This includes things like a smaller default memory footprint, giving back memory faster when not in use, putting the user in more control of pre-launch, and limiting pre-launch on devices with lower memory capacity."

— Microsoft representative

PowerToys is also getting a low-memory mode that will close idle utilities to free up RAM. But these improvements have not shipped yet, and Windows 11's idle memory consumption — hovering between 6GB and 8GB — remains a problem that no amount of marketing can paper over.

For now, the 8GB Surface devices exist in a contradiction: they carry Microsoft's brand but cannot run Microsoft's own flagship AI features. Whether the promised optimizations arrive before budget buyers start looking elsewhere may determine whether the 8GB experiment is a bridge or a dead end.
nri_angle: Rising DRAM prices driven by AI infrastructure demand affect PC buyers globally, including cost-conscious consumers in India and the diaspora market.
author: Diaspora Desk
